provision: ss 21–23 (Accountability obligations for accountable entities & accountable persons)
title: Accountability obligations for AI-enabled banking operations and accountable persons
concise_summary: Accountable entities (ADIs) and accountable persons must conduct business with honesty and integrity, with due skill, care and diligence, deal with APRA and ASIC openly and constructively, take reasonable steps to prevent matters adversely affecting prudential standing/reputation, and take reasonable steps to prevent material contravention of listed financial services/prudential laws.

title: Statutory AFSL general obligations covering efficient honest and fair conduct and technological/risk adequacy
concise_summary: An AFS licensee must do all things necessary to ensure financial services covered by the licence are provided efficiently, honestly and fairly (s 912A(1)(a)), have adequate financial/technological/human resources (s 912A(1)(d)), maintain adequate risk management systems (s 912A(1)(h)), and comply with financial services laws — underpinning non-binding ASIC RG 104 guidance.
scoping_or_legal_question: Verify Compilation currency and avoid duplicate overlap with existing guidance-layer obligations AU-ASIC-RG104-COMPLIANCE-TECH and AU-ASIC-RG104-REPRESENTATIVES prior to runtime import.

title: Notify ASIC within 30 calendar days of reasonable grounds that a reportable situation has arisen
concise_summary: AFS and credit licensees (parallel NCCP Act s 50A) must lodge a prescribed report with ASIC within 30 calendar days after first knowing or being reckless as to whether there are reasonable grounds to believe a reportable situation (core obligation significant breach or systemic failure involving AI) has arisen.
scoping_or_legal_question: Confirm cross-referencing with NCCP Act s 50A credit breach reporting and ASIC RG 78 before runtime import (ensure strict non-equivalence separation from APRA CPS 234 72h and Privacy Act 30-day NDB triggers).

provision: Part 7.8A ss 994B–994E (Design and Distribution Obligations & Target Market Determinations)
title: Design and Distribution Obligations (DDO) for AI-assisted financial product targeting and distribution
concise_summary: Issuers and distributors of retail financial and credit products must make and review a Target Market Determination (TMD) (s 994B), take reasonable steps so retail product distribution (including AI eligibility/pricing/marketing engines) is reasonably likely to be consistent with the TMD (s 994E), and notify ASIC of significant dealings inconsistent with a TMD.
scoping_or_legal_question: Confirm scope boundary between AFSL financial products and ACL credit products covered by DDO before runtime import.

instrument_title: ASIC Corporations (Internal Dispute Resolution Data Reporting) Instrument 2022/205 (as amended by 2023/282 and 2026/48)
provision: Whole instrument (Mandatory semi-annual IDR complaint data reporting to ASIC)
title: Submit mandatory six-monthly IDR complaint data reports to ASIC in the prescribed format
concise_summary: Financial firms (AFSL/ACL/RSE licensees) within scope of ASIC Instrument 2022/205 must collect prescribed complaint-level data and submit six-monthly IDR data reports to ASIC (every 6 months within prescribed lodgement windows) in the mandated ASIC schema — legally distinct from RG 271 internal systemic-issue obligations under Instrument 2020/98.
